(1) In a suit for specific performance of a contract, the plaintiff may also claim compensation for its breach 1[in addition to] such performance.

(3) If, in any such suit, the court decides that specific performance ought to be granted, but that it is not sufficient to satisfy the justice of the case, and that some compensation for breach of the contract should also be made to the plaintiff, it shall award him such compensation accordingly.
(4) In determining the amount of any compensation awarded under this section, the court shall be guided by the principles specified in section 73 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (9 of 1872).
(5) No compensation shall be awarded under this section unless the plaintiff has claimed such compensation in his plaint:
Provided that where the plaintiff has not claimed any such compensation in the plaint, the court shall, at any stage of the proceeding, allow him to amend the plaint on such terms as may be just, for including a claim for such compensation.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force Act, 1992
Purpose
•	The Act establishes the Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force (ITBPF) to ensure the security of India's borders.
Key Provisions
1.	Constitution and Control
•	Establishment: Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force (ITBPF) under Central Government.
•	Leadership: Directed by a Director-General, with support from Additional Directors-General and Inspectors-General.
2.	Definitions
•	Enemy: Includes mutineers, armed rebels, rioters, pirates, and anyone in arms against whom action is mandated.
•	Force Members: Encompasses officers, subordinate officers, under-officers, and other enrolled persons.
•	Active Duty: Service during operations against enemies, border patrols, or as declared by the Central Government.
3.	Service Conditions
•	Enrolment: Process for joining the ITBPF to be prescribed by rules.
•	Service Liability: Members can be deployed anywhere in India or abroad.
•	Tenure: Serve at the pleasure of the President of India.
4.	Powers and Protections
•	Conferred Powers: Members may be granted powers under various Central and State laws for specific duties.
•	Legal Protection: Immunity for actions taken in good faith under the Act or rules made thereunder.
5.	Administrative and Judicial Provisions
•	Rule Making Authority: Central Government empowered to make rules for the Act's implementation.
•	Judicial Proceedings: Provisions for Force Courts; civil courts generally barred from interfering in Act-related actions.

indexableObject.name: The Patents Act, 1970

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of The Patents Act, 1970
Key Provisions
1.	Term of Patent: - The term of every patent (not expired or ceased) is 20 years from the date of application filing (as per the new context, Act 2002, applicable to The Patents Act, 1970, for unexpired patents at the commencement).
2.	Grant and Rights: - Patents are granted to encourage inventions worked in India on a commercial scale.
•	Patentees have exclusive rights, but these can be subject to compulsory licensing if the invention is not worked in India or not available at a reasonably affordable price.
3.	Compulsory Licences: - Can be granted after 3 years from the patent grant date if the invention is not worked in India, not available at a reasonable price, or if the public's reasonable requirements are not met.
4.	Revocation: - Grounds include non-working of the patent in India, failure to meet public requirements, or unavailability at a reasonable price.
•	Application for revocation can be made after 2 years from the first compulsory licence grant.
5.	Working of Patents: - Emphasis on ensuring patents are worked in India to promote technological innovation and public interest, especially in vital sectors.
6.	International Arrangements: - Recognition of convention countries for patent applications.

indexableObject.name: Reporting of accidents.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
When any of the following accidents occur in the course of working an aerial ropeway for public traffic, namely:-
(a) any accident attended with loss of human life or with grievous hurt as defined in the Indian Penal Code (XLV of 1860), or with serious injury to property;
(b) any accident of a description usually attended with loss of human life or with such grievous hurt as aforesaid or with serious injury to property;
(c) any accident of any other description which the State Government may specify in this behalf in the rules, the promoter shall, without unnecessary delay, send notice of the accident to the State Government and to the Inspector and the servant of the promoter in charge of the station on the aerial ropeway nearest to the place at which the accident occurred or, where there is no station, the promoter's servant in charge of the section of the aerial ropeway on which the accident occurred, shall, with the least possible delay, give notice of the accident in Greater Bombay, to the Commissioner of Police and elsewhere to the Magistrate of the district in which the accident occurred and to the officer in charge of the police station within the local limits of which such accident occurred.

(8) If any question arises whether for the purpose of sub-section (3) any officer or other employee of the 4[Municipal Corporation] concerned was immediately before the date of constitution of the Development Authority employed exclusively in connection with the performance of functions under Chapter XIV of the Uttar Pradesh 4[Municipal Corporation] Adhiniyam, 1959, in the area for which the Development Authority is constituted it shall be referred to the State Government, whose decision shall be final and shall not be questioned in any court.

(b) if he was employed immediately before the date of the constitution of the Development Authority in a temporary capacity, equivalent to one month's salary.
